full_judgment:
4. The learned Advocate further submitted that the trial of both the scheduled and non-scheduled offences together was also illegal. 

 7. The learned Assistant Attorney-General by reference to section 29 of the Special Powers Act submitted that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, so far only as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Special Powers Act, shall apply to the proceedings of Special Tribunals. Then by reference to section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Assistant Attorney-General submitted that since the framing of charges of the scheduled and non-scheduled offences together was simply an error in regard to the framing of the charges so such error cannot be taken to be fatal for reversing or altering the conviction on appeal. 

 8. On this point Mr. Serajul Huq referred to a decision reported in 10 DLR (SC) page 29 wherein it has been held that no question as to whether prejudice was caused or not need be considered when illegality has resulted from adopting a mode of trial prohibited by the Code of Criminal Procedure. Apart from this decision when the very taking of cognizance of an offence, the framing of accusation and the trial upon charges of both scheduled and non-schedule offences together suffered from complete lack of jurisdiction, this could not at all be considered to be a mere defect in the framing of charges which by aid of section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure can be cured if prejudice is not caused to the accused. A mere defect in framing of charge by the Court having jurisdiction is one thing while the framing of charge without having any jurisdiction is a completely different thing. 

 10. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate, has referred to 3 decisions namely, those reported in 33 DLR page 203, 35 DLR page 127 and 41 DLR page 274. In all these decisions 3 different Division Benches of this Court have consistently held that joinder of scheduled and non-scheduled offences and the trial by the Special Tribunal of both scheduled and non-scheduled offences are without any lawful authority vide decision in 33 DLR page 203. 

 11. Next, it has been held in 35 DLR page 127 that the joinder of scheduled offences and non-scheduled offences was illegal and so also the cognizance taken by the Special Tribunal of both scheduled and non-scheduled offences was without jurisdiction. 

 12. Lastly, it has been held in the decision reported in 41 DLR page 274 that offences punishable under section 156(1)(8) of the Customs Act being non-scheduled offence under section 26 of the Special Powers Act the trial for both the scheduled and non-scheduled offence by the Special Tribunal is illegal. 

 17. The next decision cited by the learned Advocate is reported in 12 DLR page 90. In this case a re-trial was directed on the ground that the trial was vitiated by misjoinder of charges. So this decision supported a case of re-trial instead of a case for discharge of accused without any re-trial. 

 21. It is no doubt a misfortune of the appellant that he has been tried and convicted by a Special Tribunal without jurisdiction because of holding the trial of scheduled and non-scheduled offences together due to ignorance or oversight of the Judge concerned but the fact remains that the charge speaks of abetment of smuggling of 110 bars of gold weighing 1100 tolas valued at around Tic. 5,23,190.00. The alleged offence is undoubtedly a serious offence affecting the pecuniary interest of the country and its people. So, the accused cannot be allowed to go scot free merely because of a technical fault or mistake of the Judge concerned. Of course, the sentence of a little over three and half years of imprisonment already suffered by the appellant should not also be ignored. So, we may direct that a fresh trial be held and in such trial if the accused-appellant be at all found guilty the sentence he had suffered in the present trial should be taken into consideration if occasion arises for making conviction and imposing sentence of imprisonment if any.
